description: A VS Code theme collection inspired by CONTROL and CONTROL Resonant, featuring four color themes, custom file and product icons, and optional typography and sound effects. Unofficial fan project.
config.sounds.title: CONTROL Theme — Sounds
config.sounds.enabled: Play optional sound effects inspired by CONTROL and CONTROL Resonant. **Off by default.** Each event can be turned on or off individually under *CONTROL Theme — Sound Events*.
config.sounds.pack.auto: Follow the active theme: CONTROL Resonant uses the Resonant pack, the other themes use the Control pack.
config.sounds.pack.control: Always use the Control pack (The Oldest House).
config.sounds.pack.resonant: Always use the Resonant pack (patterned Manhattan).
config.sounds.volume: Sound volume, from 0 to 200. Above 100 the sounds are amplified (up to +6 dB) with a soft limiter, for loud music or quiet speakers.
config.sounds.onlyWithControlTheme: Only play sounds while one of the CONTROL themes is active.
config.sounds.errorTrigger: When to check for new errors.
config.sounds.errorTrigger.onSave: After saving a file (recommended: errors that appear while you type do not make noise).
config.sounds.errorTrigger.live: As soon as the error count changes, after a short pause.
config.sounds.cooldownMs: Minimum time between two sounds, in milliseconds. More important sounds (errors, failed builds) can still interrupt less important ones.
config.sounds.customFolder: Folder with your own `.wav` files. Use the same file names as the built-in packs (`startup.wav`, `theme.wav`, `save.wav`, `typing.wav`, `error.wav`, `clear.wav`, `build-ok.wav`, `build-fail.wav`, `terminal-fail.wav`, `debug.wav`, `breakpoint.wav`, `commit.wav`). Missing files fall back to the selected pack. The extension never includes or downloads third-party audio.
config.events.title: CONTROL Theme — Sound Events
config.events.themeActivated: When you switch to a CONTROL theme.
config.events.save: When you save a file manually (auto-save is ignored).
config.events.typing: While you type in the editor: a soft typewriter key (Control pack) or a resonance tick (Resonant pack). It never interrupts other sounds.
config.events.allClear: When the last error is fixed.
config.events.buildSuccess: When a task (build, test…) finishes successfully.
config.events.terminalFail: When a terminal command fails (requires shell integration).
config.events.breakpoint: When the debugger stops at a breakpoint.
config.events.gitCommit: When you make a Git commit.
config.font.title: CONTROL Theme — Typography
config.font: Typography inspired by the games for the editor, terminal, debug console, chat and Markdown preview. The fonts are installed only for your user and your previous font is restored when you choose `none`. The original game fonts are commercial, so free alternatives (SIL OFL) are used: **Overpass** (derived from Highway Gothic, like Interstate) and **Space Mono / Space Grotesk**.
config.font.none: Keep your own font (nothing is changed).
config.font.bureau: Bureau (Control): Overpass Mono and Overpass, inspired by the Bureau signage. Uses Interstate if you have it installed.
config.font.resonant: Resonant (Control Resonant): Space Mono and Space Grotesk.
config.font.auto: Follow the theme: Resonant with CONTROL Resonant, Bureau with the other CONTROL themes, your own font with any other theme.
capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces: In Restricted Mode, sound settings from the workspace are ignored: only your user settings can turn sounds on or change them.
command.applyFullSet: Apply the Full Set (Theme and Icons)…
command.declassify: Reveal/Cover Classified Values in This File
config.protocols.title: CONTROL Theme — Bureau Protocols
config.classified.enabled: **Classified mode.** Covers secret values with redaction bars (the values of `.env` files, keys and certificates, and any setting whose name looks like a secret: password, token, API key…) so you can share your screen or stream safely. Put the cursor on a line to reveal it, or click the *Classified* icon in the status bar. The file is not changed. **Off by default.**
config.classified.files: Files where Classified mode applies (glob patterns; a pattern without `/` matches in any folder). In `.env` files every value is covered; in the others, values whose name contains one of `#bureauTheme.classified.keywords#`, passwords in connection strings and URLs, and PEM keys.
config.classified.keywords: Words that mark a value as secret when they appear in its name (case, `-`, `_` and spaces are ignored: `api_key`, `ApiKey` and `API-KEY` all match `apikey`). Plain words, not regular expressions.
config.alertLevel.enabled: **Bureau alert level** in the status bar: *Clear* (no problems), *Anomaly* (warnings), *Alert* (errors) or *Hiss Incursion* (many errors). Click it to open the Problems panel. **Off by default.**
config.alertLevel.incursionThreshold: Number of errors from which the alert level becomes *Hiss Incursion*.
config.board.comments: **The Board comments** on your work in the status bar, without notifications: commits, tasks that succeed or fail, debugging sessions, the last error fixed and the first start of the day. Ask for a message at any time with **CONTROL: Message from the Board**. **Off by default.**
color.classifiedBar: Colour of the redaction bars of Classified mode (CONTROL Theme).
walkthrough.title: Welcome to the Bureau
walkthrough.description: Set up the CONTROL themes, the icons, the typography, the sounds and the Bureau protocols in a few steps. Everything is also in the Oldest House: the icon of the building in the status bar.
walkthrough.theme.title: Choose your sector
walkthrough.theme.description:
<<EVERY SECTOR OF THE HOUSE HAS ITS OWN LIGHT.>>
Four colour themes: **Dark** (the Oldest House), **Black** (OLED), **Resonant** (patterned Manhattan) and **Astral** (light).
[Choose a CONTROL theme](command:bureauTheme.chooseTheme)
walkthrough.theme.alt: The four CONTROL themes side by side: Dark, Black, Resonant and Astral.
walkthrough.fullSet.title: Requisition the full kit
walkthrough.fullSet.description:
<<AN AGENT IS ISSUED EVERYTHING AT ONCE.>>
One step applies a CONTROL theme, **Bureau Icons** for files and folders and **Bureau Product Icons** for VS Code itself. You can undo it.
[Apply the full set](command:bureauTheme.applyFullSet)
walkthrough.fullSet.alt: The Bureau badge with the Objects of Power that replace the icons of VS Code.
walkthrough.icons.title: Objects of Power in your toolbar
walkthrough.icons.description:
<<THE HOTLINE RINGS. THE DUCK LISTENS. POLARIS GUIDES.>>
File icons and the icons of VS Code redrawn from the lore: the Hotline for notifications, the rubber duck for debugging, Polaris for AI, the tape that links the Control Points for source control…
[Choose file icons](command:workbench.action.selectIconTheme)
[Choose product icons](command:workbench.action.selectProductIconTheme)
walkthrough.icons.alt: Bureau Icons for files and folders and the Bureau Product Icons.
walkthrough.followSystem.title: Light by day, dark by night
walkthrough.followSystem.description:
<<THE THRESHOLD OPENS AT DAWN AND CLOSES AT DUSK.>>
Let VS Code follow the light or dark mode of your system: CONTROL Astral in light mode and the dark theme you choose in dark mode.
[Follow the system](command:bureauTheme.followSystem)
walkthrough.followSystem.alt: The Threshold between CONTROL Astral and CONTROL Dark.
walkthrough.typography.title: The signage of the Bureau
walkthrough.typography.description:
<<THE SIGNAGE MUST BE LEGIBLE. ALWAYS.>>
Free fonts inspired by the games for the editor, the terminal and the chat, installed only for your user. Your own font is restored whenever you want.
[Choose a typography](command:bureauTheme.chooseFont)
walkthrough.typography.alt: A sample of the Bureau and Resonant typographies.
walkthrough.sounds.title: The switchboard
walkthrough.sounds.description:
<<LISTEN. THE HOUSE IS SPEAKING.>>
Optional sound effects when you save, when errors appear or disappear, when a build ends, when you debug or commit. Off by default.
[Open the sound console](command:bureauTheme.soundMenu)
walkthrough.sounds.alt: The Songmaster jukebox and a resonance wave.
walkthrough.classified.title: Classified mode
walkthrough.classified.description:
<<SOME DOCUMENTS ARE NOT FOR EVERY EYE.>>
Covers the values of `.env` files, keys, certificates and settings with secrets with redaction bars, so you can share your screen or stream safely. Put the cursor on a line to reveal it.
[Turn Classified mode on or off](command:bureauTheme.toggleClassified)
walkthrough.classified.alt: A Bureau dossier with its secret values redacted.
walkthrough.alertLevel.title: Bureau alert level
walkthrough.alertLevel.description:
<<THE BUREAU MEASURES THE THREAT. SO SHOULD YOU.>>
A status bar indicator that goes from **Clear** to **Hiss Incursion** with the errors and warnings of your workspace. Click it to open the Problems panel.
[Show or hide the alert level](command:bureauTheme.toggleAlertLevel)
walkthrough.alertLevel.alt: The Bureau alert beacon and the four alert levels.
walkthrough.board.title: Messages from the Board
walkthrough.board.description:
<<WE HAVE BEEN EXPECTING YOU.>>
The Board can speak at random moments of the day (how many times, at what hours, with its messages or yours) and comment quietly on your commits, tasks and debugging sessions. Original texts written for this theme.
[Hear the Board](command:bureauTheme.boardMessage)
[Turn random messages on or off](command:bureauTheme.toggleBoardRandom)
[Configure the Board](command:bureauTheme.boardSettings)
walkthrough.board.alt: The Board, the inverted pyramid of the Astral Plane.
command.toggleStatusBarItem: Show/Hide the Oldest House Icon in the Status Bar
config.general.title: CONTROL Theme
config.statusBarItem: Show the Oldest House icon in the status bar. Click it to open the Oldest House: colour theme, icons, typography, sounds, music and Bureau protocols, without editing `settings.json`. You can also hide it from the Oldest House itself or by right-clicking the status bar.
config.board.random: **Random messages from the Board** at any moment of the day (by default 3 a day, as a notification with *Another message* and *No more today*). Never while you debug; if VS Code is in the background, it waits until you come back. **Off by default.**
config.board.timesPerDay: How many random messages a day, spread at random over `#bureauTheme.board.hours#`.
config.board.hours: Hours for the random messages, for example `09:00-18:00` (it can cross midnight: `22:00-02:00`). Empty: any time of the day.
config.board.hours.error: Use the format 09:00-18:00, or leave it empty for the whole day.
config.board.display.notification: A notification with "Another message" and "No more today".
config.board.display.statusBar: A few seconds in the status bar, without interrupting.
config.board.source.custom: Only yours (the Board's while you have none).
config.board.customMessages: Your own messages, mixed with the Board's (for example `<<DRINK WATER, AGENT.>>`). Edit them from **CONTROL: Configure the Board…** too.
config.music.title: CONTROL Theme — Music
config.music.enabled: **Songmaster jukebox**: shows what is playing in the status bar (Spotify or any player), with play/pause, next and previous, and links to the official CONTROL soundtracks. It reads the music from the system itself — Windows media session, Spotify and Music on macOS, MPRIS on Linux — with no account and nothing leaving your computer. **Off by default.**
config.music.source.any: Any player: Spotify, the browser, Apple Music, VLC… (on macOS, Spotify and Music).
config.music.controls: Show the previous, play/pause and next buttons next to the song.
walkthrough.music.title: The Songmaster jukebox
walkthrough.music.description:
<<THE JUKEBOX REMEMBERS EVERY SONG.>>
What is playing in Spotify or any player, in the status bar with its controls. No account and nothing leaves your computer. And the official soundtracks of both games, one click away.
[Turn the jukebox on or off](command:bureauTheme.toggleMusic)
[Listen to the CONTROL soundtrack](command:bureauTheme.openSoundtrack?%5B%22control%22%5D)
[Listen to the CONTROL Resonant soundtrack](command:bureauTheme.openSoundtrack?%5B%22resonant%22%5D)
walkthrough.music.alt: The Songmaster jukebox, a vinyl record and the song in the status bar.

config.terminal.title: CONTROL Theme — Bureau Terminal
config.terminal.prompt: **Bureau terminal prompt** for PowerShell, cmd, bash, zsh and fish, without Oh My Posh or Nerd Fonts. New VS Code terminals open with it (the *Bureau* profile) and the prompt changes at once in the terminals already open. The icons come from **Bureau Prompt Icons**, a font installed only for your user and added behind your terminal font. cmd only shows the folder, colours and the time. **Off by default.**
config.terminal.prompt.signage: Signage: solid blocks like the signs of the Oldest House (system, folder, Git branch, time and error).
config.terminal.prompt.dossier: Dossier: two lines framed like a Bureau case file, ending in the Control Point.
config.terminal.prompt.controlPoint: Control Point: minimal; the Point empties when a command fails.
config.terminal.prompt.board: The Board: <<IN ITS VOICE.>> (WITH ITS ECHOES.), and a Board message when the terminal opens.
config.terminal.prompt.alertLevel: Alert level: Clear, Anomaly, Alert or Hiss Incursion on the right, with the time.
config.terminal.classified: **Classified** in the terminal: the prompt of each command you run is covered with a redaction bar (folder and branch), handy for streaming. PowerShell, zsh and fish.
config.terminal.icons: Show icons in the prompt (the **Bureau Prompt Icons** font). Off: text only, for terminals that cannot use the font (such as the classic Windows console).
config.terminal.windowsIcon.controlPoint: Four Control Points: the four windows as the squares of the Git branch.
config.terminal.windowsIcon.house: The House with windows: the windowless monolith of the Oldest House, with four.
config.terminal.macosIcon.command: ⌘ of the tape: four Control Points joined by a ring.
config.terminal.macosIcon.apple: Octagonal apple: drawn with the Bureau geometry, without curves.
config.terminal.linuxIcon: System icon on Linux (also a shell in WSL or over SSH).
config.terminal.linuxIcon.tux: Bureau Tux: octagons, square eyes and belly.
config.terminal.linuxIcon.tuxMop: Tux with Ahti's mop: Linux was born in Finland, like the janitor of the Bureau.
config.terminal.commandFrame: A header and a closing line for each command you run (npm, git…): the command and the time when it starts, the result and how long it took when it ends. PowerShell, bash, zsh and fish; not for `cd` or `clear`.
config.terminal.gitColors: The output of Git (`git status`, `log`, `branch`, `diff`) in the colours of the Bureau, in the shells with the Bureau prompt: the branch in the accent, changes in amber, untracked files in grey, remote branches in cyan and tags in magenta. The colours you set in your own Git configuration come first. Needs Git 2.31 or later.
config.terminal.newTerminals: With the prompt on, the **Bureau** terminal profile becomes the default of VS Code, so new terminals open with it. Your previous default comes back when you turn it off.
config.terminal.shell: Shell of the **Bureau** terminal profile. `auto` uses the shell of your previous default terminal (or the one of your system). bash on Windows is Git Bash.
config.terminal.shell.auto: Automatic: the shell of your previous default terminal.
walkthrough.terminal.title: The Bureau terminal
walkthrough.terminal.description:
<<THE PROMPT IS A DOOR. MARK IT.>>
A prompt for PowerShell, cmd, bash, zsh and fish in five Bureau styles, with the icon of your system and Classified mode, without Oh My Posh. You can also take it outside VS Code.
[Choose the prompt](command:bureauTheme.chooseTerminalPrompt)
[Open a Bureau terminal](command:bureauTheme.newBureauTerminal)
[More options](command:bureauTheme.terminalMenu)
walkthrough.terminal.alt: A terminal with the Bureau prompt: the system icon, the folder, the Git branch and the Control Point.
